A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MixtureVitae study. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and complete appendices are readable and matchable, including material moved between sections.

before.justification: V2 reports original controlled pretraining experiments, benchmark evaluations, component ablations, red-teaming results and contamination analyses.

after.justification: V5 retains these original results and adds CommonsenseQA evaluation, an instruction-tuned comparator and further retraining controls.

M1.justification: Section 2.2.6 changes the stated synthetic-source eligibility rule from exclusively permissive seeds and generators to prioritizing them while admitting Tier 2(b) exceptions. The provenance scheme gains corresponding subtiers. This revises the reported curation policy; the PDFs do not establish newly introduced sources. Architectures, single-stage pretraining, deduplication, packing and procedural math generation remain unchanged.

E1.justification: V5 adds CommonsenseQA to the evaluated language-understanding suite. Existing math, code, instruction-following and safety tasks remain. The doubled corpus token count and finer breakdown of previously aggregated sources do not establish additional training domains; multilingual expansion remains future work.

E2.justification: V5 Table 2 adds SmolLM2-1.7B-Instruct while retaining SmolLM2-1.7B and the existing dataset baselines. V2's abstract already mentions an instruction-tuned comparison, but its corresponding Table 1 reports only the base SmolLM2 row. Apertus remains a discussion comparison without reported evaluation against MixtureVitae.

E3.justification: The reported training corpus changes from 211.1B to 422B tokens, without explaining whether this reflects additional data or corrected counting. V5 specifies 10-shot CommonsenseQA and an eleven-task aggregate, although some passages still say ten tasks. It also introduces full flagged-document removal followed by 1.7B-model retraining for 300B tokens and a Tier 2(b) exclusion control. Existing architecture and training-schedule tables remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V5 adds retraining after removing every document flagged by the contamination scan (Appendix D, Figure 10), extending v2's clean-test-set evaluation and three-shard removal experiment. Appendix I and Figure 11 newly test dependence on restricted or opaque Tier 2(b) sources. Existing component ablations, scaling analyses and red-teaming results are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-seed summaries, confidence intervals or formal significance tests. Existing three-point moving-average curves are retained, and the added controls do not introduce uncertainty estimates or repeated-run reporting.

E6.justification: New CommonsenseQA scores include 0.49 for MixtureVitae versus 0.21 for Comma-0.1 and 0.20 for DCLM. The added SmolLM2-Instruct row reports GSM8K/HumanEval/MBPP scores of 0.37/0.28/0.37. New controls report slightly better performance after full decontamination and nearly unchanged performance without Tier 2(b). Corpus totals and licensing-tier proportions also change. Existing math/code rows and clean-test-set results are retained; eleven-task averages are not same-setting improvements over a stated ten-task aggregate.

T1.justification: The contamination coverage and leakage-percentage formulas, computational estimates and procedural math example remain unchanged. V5 introduces no new theorem, proof, formal assumption or mathematical derivation; its expanded licensing taxonomy is nonmathematical.

C1.justification: The central claim that reasoning-dense, permissive-first pretraining can compete with mixed-license corpora is retained, as is the abstract's instruction-tuned comparison. V5 advertises a 422B-token corpus and adds explicit claims about preserving core language understanding and providing a reusable, scalable pretraining blueprint.

C2.justification: V5 qualifies the earlier exclusive-permissiveness account by identifying approximately 4% restricted or opaque synthetic provenance and interpreting its removal as quality-neutral. Expanded Appendices F and I discuss generator restrictions, ambiguous P3 licenses, EU opt-outs and copyright reproduction risks. Appendix D newly acknowledges that exact matching misses paraphrases, while Appendix J discusses English-centric coverage and untested scaling directions.

D1.justification: New Table 14 provides source-level licenses, generator permissiveness, seed provenance, token counts and exclusions for previously aggregated synthetic components. Additional text clarifies shard organization and domain-aware packing. Conversely, v5 removes the explicit uniform-sampling and repeated-sampling description from Section 3.1. The code link is retained; release timing remains inconsistent between present-release claims and Section 6's promise of release upon acceptance.

R1.justification: New Section 4.4 positions the work relative to Akter et al.'s front-loading study and Wang et al.'s thinking-augmented pretraining. The brief Apertus availability note becomes a substantive comparison of scale, language coverage, inclusion strategy and artifact distribution. Additional opt-out and scaling references support this positioning; routine bibliographic corrections are separate.

P1.justification: The contribution list, results commentary and conclusion undergo extensive rewriting. Existing appendix evidence is integrated into a new main-text decontamination section, the legal discussion is reorganized into subsections, and domain lists are consolidated. These changes substantially restructure the narrative beyond simply adding experiments or renumbering sections.

P2.justification: V5 adds the main benchmark summary table, a full-page provenance table and two control figures. V2 Table 9 and Figure 9 move into the main text as Table 3 and Figure 4. Composition charts are rescaled and revised, Figure 3 is redrawn, and several captions and table highlights change. Existing appendix benchmark and scaling plots retain their graphical content.

improvement.justification: V5 strengthens evidential support through full flagged-document retraining, the Tier 2(b) ablation and an explicit instruction-tuned comparator, while Table 14 substantially improves provenance disclosure. These extend v2's existing validation rather than overturning its findings. The net gain is limited by the unexplained corpus-count revision, inconsistent ten/eleven-task reporting and retained blanket permissive-source statements despite newly documented exceptions.
